{{Short description|Computer scientist and mathematician in New Zealand}}
'''Bakhadyr M. Khoussainov''' ({{langx|ru|Бахадыр Хусаинов}})<ref>{{Cite news |title=Бахадыр Хусаинов |pages=134 |work=Новая Зеландия говорит по-русски 2013 |url=https://rusnewsnz.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/1-Book_21-10-2013-otpravleno-for-printing-24-10-13.pdf}}</ref> is a [[computer scientist]] and [[mathematician]], who was born and educated in the [[Soviet Union]], works in the fields of [[mathematical logic]], [[computability theory]], [[computable model theory]] and [[theoretical computer science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=People – Algorithms and Logic Group in UESTC |url=https://tcsuestc.com/people/ |access-date=2022-04-30 |language=en-US}}</ref> With [[Anil Nerode]], he is the co-founder of the theory of automatic structures,<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Khoussainov |first1=Bakhadyr |last2=Nerode |first2=Anil |title=Logic and Computational Complexity |chapter=Automatic presentations of structures |date=1995 |editor-last=Leivant |editor-first=Daniel |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-60178-3_93 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |volume=960 |pages=367–392 |doi=10.1007/3-540-60178-3_93 |isbn=978-3-540-44720-7}}</ref> which is an extension of the theory of [[automatic group]]s.

== Biography ==
Khoussainov received his undergraduate degree from the Mathematics Department of [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 1984. In 1988, he received his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree (equivalent to a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]) in Algebra and Logic from [[Novosibirsk State University]] with the supervision of an Academician of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] {{interlanguage link|Sergei Goncharov|ru|Гончаров,_Сергей_Савостьянович}}.

In 1991 Khoussainov joined [[Cornell University]] and held an H.C. Wang Assistant Professorship at the Mathematics Department from 1995 to 1997.

In 1996 Khoussainov joined the [[University of Auckland]], and remained until 2021 when he moved to the [[University of Electronic Science and Technology of China|UESTC]].

Khoussainov has held visiting positions at [[Cornell University]], the [[University of Chicago]], the [[National University of Singapore]], [[Kyoto University]], [[Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology|JAIST]] and the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]].

== Awards and recognition ==
Khoussainov is a co-winner (together with [[Cristian S. Calude|Cristian Calude]], Sanjay Jain, Wei Li and Frank Stephan) of the [[Symposium on Theory of Computing|STOC]] 2017 best paper award<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACM SIGACT - STOC Best Paper Award |url=https://www.sigact.org/prizes/best_paper.html |access-date=2021-02-06 |website=www.sigact.org}}</ref> for a [[quasi-polynomial time]] algorithm deciding [[parity game]]s. For this work, Khoussainov and this paper's co-authors were awarded the 2021 EATCS-IPEC [[Nerode Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPEC Nerode Prize |url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/nerode-prize}}</ref> In 2023 while working in the UESTC, China, Khoussainov has also been elected as a foreign member of The [[Academia Europaea]], the European Academy of Sciences, Humanities, Letters, and Law.

A fellow of the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi|Royal Society of New Zealand]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=View our current Fellows|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/view-our-fellows/|access-date=2021-02-06|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> Khoussainov has also received: 

* the 2020 [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt prize]];<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bakh Khoussainov receives Humboldt Research Award {{!}} New Zealand Association of von Humboldt Fellows |url=https://www.humboldt.org.nz/2019/11/27/new-humboldt-research-award/ |access-date=2021-02-06 |website=www.humboldt.org.nz |archive-date=2021-02-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211055733/https://www.humboldt.org.nz/2019/11/27/new-humboldt-research-award/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* the 2019 Aitken Lecturership;<ref>{{Cite web |title=LMS-NZMS Forder and Aitken Lectureships of London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/events/lectures/forder-and-aitken-lectureship |access-date=2021-02-06 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>
* multiple [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science|JSPS]] Invitation Fellowships (2001, 2012, and 2014);<ref>{{Cite web |title=Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan {{!}} Japan Society for the Promotion of Science |url=https://www.jsps.go.jp/english/e-inv/index.html |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=www.jsps.go.jp}}</ref>
* multiple [[Marsden grant|Marsden Fund]] grants (2001, 2004, 2008 and 2012);<ref>{{Cite web|title=Search Marsden awards 2008–2017|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/marsden/awarded-grants/search-marsden-awards/|access-date=2021-02-06|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>
* the 2002 Research Excellence Award of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Mathematical Society : Awards and Prizes |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards |access-date=2021-02-06 |website=nzmathsoc.org.nz}}</ref>
